title: Pump the Right Tank
summary: Mrs. Alabi can only top up one tank before the weekend rush. Petrol and Diesel sell the most litres — but is that where the money is?

client.name: Mrs. Funke Alabi
brief: The tanker only has room to refill one tank before Friday traffic hits the Gateway road. Petrol and Diesel move the most litres by far, so my pump attendants want those topped up first.
But Premium has a much thinner stock and a much fatter margin. Litres sold isn't the same as naira earned — tell me which tank actually makes us the most money.
client.thanks: Premium. I'd have burned the weekend's profit refilling the wrong tank if you hadn't checked the margins.

starterSql:
-- Which fuel actually earns the most profit?
-- Careful: price_per_litre isn't profit — subtract what it cost first.

SELECT *
FROM fuel_sales
LIMIT 20;

tables.name: fuel_sales
tables.description: Every pump sale at Atlas Fuel station this week.

columns.name: price_per_litre
columns.desc: What the customer paid per litre, in naira (₦)

columns.name: cost_per_litre
columns.desc: What the station paid the supplier per litre, in naira (₦)

hints.title: Hint 1: Price isn't profit
hints.desc: A sale's profit is (price_per_litre − cost_per_litre) × litres — the margin on every litre sold, not just how much changed hands.

hints.title: Hint 2: Litres sold tells a different story
hints.desc: Ranking by SUM(litres) alone will point at whichever fuel moves the most volume, even if its margin is thin.

hints.title: Hint 3: Sum the real profit per fuel
hints.desc: GROUP BY fuel_type, SUM the per-sale profit, and take the top one.

findings.claim: Which fuel should get the one tanker refill?

options.text: Diesel — it sells the most litres this week
Premium — far fewer litres, but a much bigger margin per litre
Petrol — tied with Diesel for the most volume

findings.claim: Why did the pump attendants' advice point the wrong way?

options.text: They were going by litres sold, not how much profit each litre actually earns.
Premium's sales aren't in the system.
They weren't wrong — Diesel really earns the most.

successFeedback: Petrol and Diesel sell in bulk, but on a thin margin. Premium sells far fewer litres at a much bigger markup — once you multiply it out, it's the tank making the real money this week.

fixtures.failHint: Your answer doesn't match the fuel with the most total profit here.
A fuel sold in small volume can still earn the most profit. Multiply margin by litres per sale, don't just total litres.

fixtures.purpose: A different week where a different fuel is the hidden earner
fixtures.failHint: Your query gives the wrong fuel on a different week's data — it may be hardcoded instead of computing the profit.
